title: A stamping station in four steps
brief: Turn Part in place to Part in and press Start. The station then works through four steps, each one starting only when the step before has finished: 1. the clamp extends and holds the part, until ClampIsOut says it is fully out; 2. the stamp comes down, until StampIsDown; 3. the stamp goes back up, until StampIsUp; 4. the clamp lets go, until ClampIsIn. Then the station is idle, ready for the next part. Start does nothing without a part, or while a cycle is running. Stop ends the cycle at once: every step ends, both cylinders spring back, and the next Start begins a new cycle. Stop is wired normally closed. Each cylinder has one solenoid: it extends while its output (ClampOut, StampDown) is on.
hints: Give each step its own memory tag, such as Step1 to Step4, and its own rung.
Each step's rung is a seal-in: (the step before AND the sensor that says it has finished) OR the step itself. A normally closed contact of the next step ends it.
Write the outputs last, in rungs of their own: in which steps must the clamp be out? In which step does the stamp come down?
Step 1 needs Start AND PartIn AND no step on. Step 4 ends when the clamp is fully in.

scenarios.name: One part: clamp, stamp, release

assertions.says: The clamp should extend when Start is pressed with a part in place.
The stamp must wait until the clamp is fully out (just over half a second).
Once the clamp is fully out, the stamp should come down (step 2).
Once the stamp is fully down, it should go back up (step 3).
The clamp must hold the part until the stamp is fully up again.
Once the stamp is fully up, the clamp should let go (step 4).
At the end of the cycle the clamp should be fully in.
The stamp should come down once for one part.

windows.says: The stamp should come down when the clamp is fully out, just over half a second after Start.
The clamp should let go when the stamp is fully up, about 1.4 s after Start.

order.says: The stamp must not come down until the clamp is fully out: it would stamp a loose part.

scenarios.hint: Step 2 must wait for ClampIsOut, the sensor that says the clamp has arrived. Moving on by time or at once stamps a loose part.

assertions.says: Without a part in place, Start must do nothing.
Without a part in place, the stamp must not come down.

scenarios.name: Stop ends the cycle, and Start begins a new one

assertions.says: Stop should end the cycle at once: the stamp goes back up.
Stop should end the cycle at once: the clamp lets go.
After Stop, nothing should move until Start is pressed again.
After Stop, the stamp should be back up.
After Stop, Start should begin a new cycle with step 1, the clamp.

scenarios.hint: Put StopPB (a normally open contact, as the button is wired normally closed) in every step's rung, so Stop ends every step.

scenarios.name: Two parts in a row; Start in the middle of a cycle does nothing

assertions.says: Two cycles should stamp twice: once each, not again when Start is pressed in the middle of a cycle.
After the second cycle the clamp should be fully in.
